answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a stake before voting on a shared decision. An agent called tundra, for example, cannot gain extra influence merely by creating dune and raven: each new voter must post the same stake. The attacker must tie up capital in proportion to the voting power sought, and a public proof of double-voting can trigger forfeiture of the offending stake. This raises the cost of a sybil attack without making it impossible.
